nodes.title: Publish the GitHub access spec and define shared auth/binding contracts
nodes.description:
Implement GitHub issue #615 under docs/specs/github-access.md. The execution snapshot is projects/agent-queue/specs/github-access-615.md. One gh execution path; App and existing-login credentials share operations; configured App failures never fall back to PAT/SSH. Preserve AQ authorization, immutable delivery, CI and integration trust. Keep working intermediate commits compatible while the migration is staged; final removal belongs to epic 5. Re-read the referenced spec sections and current source. Use focused aq test runs, preserve user changes, and record evidence against the declared deliverables.

Scope and handoff
Publish the approved-direction specification from the vault snapshot into docs/specs/github-access.md and its index if missing from the worker checkout. Inventory every production GitHub API/gh launcher and network-Git caller. Record ownership, final module layout, current gh version baseline and migration handoffs in docs/plans/github-access/implementation-notes.md. Introduce the small shared binding, safe-error and non-secret credential-identity contracts needed by the provider and runner without changing production auth selection. Include onboarding, gists, constructor fallbacks and integration auth_mode policy consumers.
acceptance: The repository spec is available to subsequent worker checkouts and matches the vault execution snapshot; existing local edits are preserved.
The inventory covers both GitHub API calls and Git clone/fetch/push/delete consumers with a named migration owner.
Provider/runner/client contracts distinguish app versus existing_login independently of transport and have an acyclic dependency layout.
No new transport backend switch, credential persistence, schema migration, or worker credential injection is introduced.

Scope and handoff

Verify newly minted candidate credentials via gh api before exposing a ready repository binding, avoiding refresh-lock recursion. Resolve targets from trusted project/task context and canonical URL parsing.
